scope: Full independent reading of all 17 conditions and solutions, alternative exact arithmetic/system checks and Kazakh ambiguity/unit review. No edition verifier or source archive was used.

entries.notes: 140 LEDs would make 20 seven-LED signs; 3/5 of that capacity is 12. Allocation 84 is integral and has no remainder. Condition and all solution steps agree.
7 shares correspond to 21 stops, so the five remaining shares contain 15. The total 36 and all stated fractions are consistent. The target is clearly unmarked stops.

entries.method: capacity subtraction on a common physical unit
entries.notes: The initial stock is 48 two-metre blanks. The two original-stock allocations consume 15 and 14 blank equivalents;48−15−14=19. Both fractions explicitly refer to the same whole, so no sequential-fraction ambiguity.
Convert stocks to 2750 g and 1625 g and use 375 g per item:2750+1625−10×375=625 g. All mixed-number equalities and kg/g units in the solution are correct.
With denominator 40, the page difference is(240×15−180×16)/40=18. The text clearly distinguishes the two book lengths; Daniyar does read more, as asked.

Enumerated positive integer ticket totals whose sold share is integral and whose unsold-minus-sold difference is 48. Unique total 120; sold 36 and unsold 84. Complementary groups and question are unambiguous.
The nested group is 25×30/10000=3/40 of all 320 pupils, giving 24. The second percentage explicitly applies only to the robotics group. Solution and participant counts are integral.
Enumerated positive prices satisfying 4 P/5+1200=10800; unique price 12000. Delivery is a separate fixed fee and is removed before undoing the discount. Every displayed equality is valid.
120%×85%=102% of the original price. The excess is 2% of 9600=192; final price 9792 exceeds the original, matching the question direction. Both percentage bases are explicit.
For final percentage c,400 c=300×8, giving c=6. Salt mass 24 g stays fixed while total mass becomes 400 g. No evaporation/salt loss is explicitly excluded in the statement; solution and units agree.
The requested budget gap is(5−3)/(3+5+4) of 36000=6000. All three component amounts sum back to 36000. The order of the named categories is explicit.
Enumerated x>0 with the second collection x+18 and 7 x=4(x+18); x=24,second 42,total 66. The larger group and mass unit are clearly specified.

After 3 days, the original group has 12 days of stock left. Scaling for 32 instead of 24 pupils gives 12×24/32=9 days. Constant per-pupil daily consumption is stated, and the answer is exactly a whole number.
The first device runs 4 minutes and the second runs 7:18×4+24×7=240 caps. This independently confirms the solution grouped by time interval. The stopped device and remaining work period are clear.
Enumerated common unit prices dividing 3120 and 1820 with purchaser counts differing by 5; unique price 260,counts 12 and 7. Same per-marker pricing and currency units are explicit.

For t minutes after the second departure,4(t+30)/60+3 t/60=23. The unique positive integral t is 180; distances 14 km and 9 km sum to 23. The time origin, opposing directions and steady speeds are explicit.
Total time is 36×2×15/(15²−3²)=5 h. Individual legs are 2 h downstream and 3 h upstream; both water-relative speeds are positive. Stops are excluded and the return endpoint is clear.
